implementation_notes: A JavaScript class method is already the one-liner - cancel(id) { return this.#repo.cancel(id); } - and the read-only attribute form is a getter, get count() { return this.#repo.count; }; because arguments are positional, the message-pattern formatting half of the pattern collapses into keeping the body on one line. Nothing replaces the named method for callers, and bulk-forwarding substitutes (prototype mixins, Object.assign, Proxy) erase the per-operation names the pattern exists for, so they are reserved for generated shims. Keep one-liners on the prototype rather than as bound per-instance fields unless the receiver must survive extraction.
pitfalls: A one-line method used as a callback loses its receiver (const f = svc.cancel; f(id) throws on this): bind it explicitly or pass an arrow that keeps the call in place.
Arrow functions in class fields create one function per instance instead of sharing the prototype method, changing memory use and super/instance behaviour.
A forwarding getter is re-evaluated on every access and cannot be destructured once to cache the value; repeated reads of an expensive delegate pay every time.
